chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Benny Payne's Cotton Club trio and Mattie Hite
summary: Before Calloway Payne sang in a trio at the Cotton Club and accompanied cabaret star Mattie Hite, earning big tips.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But, you see, -- How that happened, you see, Benny used to sing with the trio up at the Cotton Club before Calloway's band even went in there. He used to sing -- they had a trio, a men's trio that used to sing up there.
One of the guys that was in the trio did Uncle Remus, the picture. Jimmy --
He was in the trio with Benny Payne.
And the other piano player -- I forget the man that played the piano in that trio.

Anyway, they used to sing in between dance sets and everything. They used to entertain, you see. And, of course, Benny before that, Benny used to accompany Mattie Hite, who was one of the greatest entertainers that ever hit New York. A cabaret singer and Benny was her accompanist. They used to make -- In those days they made $200 a night tips.
